algorithm.teacherCuratedHint: No auto-assignment — you assign students by hand.

matchingInfo.ballotWorkflowIntro: After students submit ranked preferences, this panel summarizes who submitted, who is matched, and splits students into two review queues.
matchingInfo.ballotSummary: The header counts show submitted ballots, matched students, and how many sit in each queue (project-first vs team-first).
matchingInfo.queueProjectFirstExplain: Project-first queue — students who did not rank classmates. Process these first.
matchingInfo.queueTeamFirstExplain: Team-first queue — students who ranked classmates. Review mutual picks here.
matchingInfo.mutualClassmatesExplain: Mutual means both students ranked each other. One-way means only one student ranked the other. Received counts classmates who ranked this student but were not ranked back.
matchingInfo.manualAssignExplain: When the round uses teacher-curated matching, each unmatched student row shows an Assign to opportunity dropdown ranked by the same scoring formula the automatic algorithms use.
matchingInfo.connectMigration: Matching algorithm selection and Run matching currently live in Connect → Matches. Matches computed there appear on this screen. Those controls are moving into Student Ranking here.
matchingInfo.intro: Three modes are available. All three share the same scoring foundation; they differ in how they assign students to opportunities once every pair has a score.
matchingInfo.scoreFormulaIntro: Every student-opportunity pair gets a score from the student's submitted preference:
matchingInfo.rankBonusExplain: rankBonus = max(0, totalOpps − rank + 1). In a 5-opportunity round, rank #1 gives a bonus of 5, #2 gives 4, unranked gives 0. Star rating is 0–5. So an opportunity ranked #1 with 5★ scores 5×10 + 5×2 = 60; the same opportunity ranked #3 with 3★ scores 36. Rank dominates stars by roughly 5:1.
matchingInfo.teamCoherence: Team coherence bonus: both automatic algorithms add +5 per mutual team-preference pair already placed on the same opportunity. Both students must nominate each other for the same opportunity for the bonus to apply. Nudges the matcher to keep mutual pairs together on team projects without forcing it.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingGuarantee: Guarantee: the assignment is stable. No student-opportunity pair would both rather be matched to each other than to their current partners.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingStep1: Sort each student's opportunities by their own preference score, highest first.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingStep2: Every unassigned student proposes to their next unproposed opportunity.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingStep3: Each opportunity keeps the top studentCapacity proposers by score and rejects the rest.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingStep4: Rejected students return to the worklist and propose to their next choice. Repeat until nobody has a pending proposal.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingExampleTitle: Micro-example — Alice, Bob, Carol; Opps X and Y (each cap 1). All three rank X first, Y second.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingExample1: Round 1: all three propose to X. X keeps the highest scorer (Bob, 60), rejects Alice (55) and Carol (50).
matchingInfo.stableMatchingExample2: Round 2: Alice and Carol propose to Y. Y keeps Alice (44), rejects Carol (40).
matchingInfo.stableMatchingExample3: Round 3: Carol has no more options → unmatched.
matchingInfo.stableMatchingPick: Pick this when you want a defensible answer if a student asks "why didn't I get X?" — the answer is always "someone ranked X higher, and we couldn't offer you your second choice without displacing them." Best for contested opportunities with heavy preference overlap.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedGuarantee: Guarantee: each individual placement maximizes score at the moment it's made. Does not guarantee stability — you can end up with pairs that would both rather swap.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedStep1: Flatten every (student, opportunity, score) triple into one list.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedStep2: Sort by descending score. Tie-break by lower preference rank.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedStep3: Walk the sorted list: skip if the student is already matched or the opportunity is full; otherwise place them.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedExample: Micro-example — same three students and opps as above. Sorted global list: (Bob,X,60) → (Alice,X,55) → (Carol,X,50) → (Carol,Y,45) → …. Bob→X. Alice/Carol at X skipped (full). Carol→Y. Alice already skipped for X, and now Y is full → unmatched.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedResult: Result: Bob→X, Carol→Y, Alice unmatched. Note this differs from stable matching — Alice ended up unmatched here even though she would have preferred Y.
matchingInfo.scoreBasedPick: Pick this when you want maximum transparency — every placement is defensible with a single number. Simple, fast, deterministic. Slightly less stable than Gale-Shapley in edge cases.
matchingInfo.teacherCuratedBody1: The algorithm intentionally produces zero matches. Every student with submitted preferences appears unmatched; you assign them by hand.
matchingInfo.teacherCuratedBody2: What still runs: the same scoring formula powers the ranked dropdowns ("Alice — rank 1, 5★") and the Propose top candidates button on each opportunity in Connect → Matches. You see the same numbers the auto-matchers would use — ranking is not hidden, just not enforced.
matchingInfo.teacherCuratedPick: Pick this when you have context the algorithm can't see (a specific mentor requested a specific student, an accessibility accommodation, a prior collaboration), OR when you want to run one of the automatic algorithms first, then flip to teacher-curated to hand-adjust the wrong placements. Switching does not delete existing matches.
matchingInfo.footerClass: New rounds default to stable matching. Algorithm selection and Run matching currently live in Connect → Matches; those controls are moving to Student Ranking here. Existing proposed and active matches are preserved when you switch algorithms.
matchingInfo.footerConnect: You can switch between algorithms at any time using the dropdown at the top of the Connect Matches page — existing proposed and active matches are preserved either direction.
